sentences.text:
Heard Sri Arvind Kumar, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Arvind Kumar
Pandey, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the State and perused the
records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing
Case Crime No.214 of 2023, under Sections 376/504/506 I.P.C. and Section 3 (2) (V) of Scheduled
Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, registered at Police Station
Kotwali Nagar, District Barabanki.

entities.text:
Police Station
Kotwali Nagar, District Barabanki
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3.  The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of a F.I.R. lodged on 19.02.2023 against the applicant and his parents, stating that the informant was in love with the applicant for the past eight years and the applicant kept on exploiting her physically under the allurement of marrying her.
Subsequently, the applicant's marriage has been settled with some other girl.

sentences.text: 1 the applicant has declined to marry the informant and when she went to his home his parents had abused her and used caste based words.
4. In the statements of the informant recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C. she has reiterated the F.I.R. version.
It has also been submitted that the names of the parents of the applicant have been expunged by the Investigating Officer during investigation.

5. In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail-application it has been contended that the applicant is innocent, he has no criminal history and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.

6. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and raised a preliminary objection that the application for anticipatory bail cannot be entertained as the F.I.R. involves allegation of offence under Section 3 (2) (V) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant while replying to the aforesaid preliminary objection has submitted that the allegation of offence under Section 3 (2) (V) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 was not levelled against the applicant and it was levelled against the applicant's parents only.
Moreover, the allegation could not be substantiated during investigation and the applicant's parents have already been exonerated.

He has submitted that although a charge sheet has been submitted against the applicant mentioning Section 3 (2) (V) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989,
no such allegation has been levelled by the informant against the applicant either in the F.I.R. or in her statement recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C.

In support of his submissions, learned counsel for the applicant has relied upon a decision of Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Prithvi Raj Chauhan Vs. Union of India: 2020 (4) SCC 727.
8.

entities.text: Prithvi Raj Chauhan Vs. Union of India: 2020 (4) SCC 727
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As there is no allegation against the applicant which may make out commission of offence under Section 3 (2) (V) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989,
I am of the view that the application can be entertained by this court.

9. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the applicant herself has stated that she was in love with the applicant for the past eight years;
that there is no allegation which may prima facie indicate that the intention of the applicant was to decieve the informant since inception, coupled with the fact that the applicant is a young man of about 24 years having no criminal history and without making any observations which may affect the outcome of the case
, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
10. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
